Dear Dr Clayton,

RE: Ms Tracy Bowen
DOB: 22/7/1988

I am writing to refer Ms Bowen, a married patient who has symptoms and signs suggestive of polycystic
ovary syndrome, for assessment and management.

Ms Bowen has a history of childhood asthma for which she was prescribed salbutamol inhaler and                Commented [AH1]: a
beclomethasone. Please note, her father was a heavy smoker.

In 2004, Concerning her menstrual history, she has had irregular infrequent menstrual periods associated
with dysmenorrhea since her menarche. As a result, she was prescribed oral contraceptive pills. A year
later, she has complained of a deep acne over her face, upper back and neck, complicated with scarring.
Consequently, she was referred to a dermatologist for treatment.

Today, she came to my practice complaining of inability to conceive. Despite stopping her contraceptive       Commented [AH2]: an
pills, she had amenorrhea, depression and weight gain. On examination, her BMI was 28 as well as              Commented [AH3]: having ceased
hirsutism which was managed by electrolysis. Furthermore, her blood tests revealed an increase in fasting     Commented [AH4]: has
blood glucose level, prolactin level and free androgen index. In addition, a decrease in vitamin D and SHBG   Commented [AH5]: , and she has
levels. Consequently, Climen was prescribed and a pelvic ultrasound was ordered.                              Commented [AH6]: is being

In view of the above, it would be highly appreciated if you could see and manage her. Please do not
hesitate to contact me for any queries.

Yours sincerely,

Dr
